summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.

key_cases.case_name: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services v. Iowa District Court for Polk County
key_cases.holding: A juvenile court acts within its authority under Iowa Code section 232.102(1)(b)(1) when, at an interested party's request, it temporarily stays HHS from moving a child in its custody until it can hold an evidentiary hearing; review of an HHS placement decision may be prospective as well as retrospective.
key_cases.relevance: Arose from HHS's attempt to move a child to a sibling placement, and addresses the statutory sibling-placement preference against the child's individual best interests.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court "shall give deference" to HHS's placement decision, but deference does not mean blind acceptance that freezes the juvenile court out of any meaningful review of HHS's decision.

key_cases.holding: The Iowa ICWA placement preferences in chapter 232B are unconstitutional as applied in voluntary termination cases, so the federal ICWA preferences and their 'good cause' exception for a parent's request govern; a tribe may also appear through a non-lawyer authorized representative.
key_cases.relevance: Determines which placement-preference hierarchy applies to an Indian child — federal, not Iowa — in voluntary proceedings, and preserves the 'good cause' deviation.
key_cases.quote: The Iowa ICWA placement preferences are unconstitutional in voluntary termination cases.

key_cases.holding: Under the 2020 Guardianship Act, when a parent revokes consent and the basis for a minor's guardianship no longer exists, Iowa Code section 232D.503(2) places the burden on the guardian to justify continuing it, and the constitutionally grounded parental preference survived the repeal of the old statutory preference; termination of the guardianship was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes that a kinship guardian cannot retain a child against a fit parent's wishes merely because the placement has become comfortable.
key_cases.quote: The constitutionally based parental preference predated section 633.559 and, in our view, survives its repeal.

key_cases.holding: Termination of a neglectful mother's rights to her ten-year-old son was affirmed; although Iowa prefers to keep siblings together and values family integrity, those preferences yield to clear and convincing evidence that the child's best interests require a permanent, stable adoptive home.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Iowa statement of the sibling-placement preference and its limits when weighed against permanency.
key_cases.quote: However, this preference is not absolute. Our ultimate concern is the best interests of the child.

key_cases.holding: Termination of parental rights to an Indian child was affirmed: the tribe was notified immediately, active efforts to prevent the breakup of the Indian family were made, and the Iowa ICWA requirements including qualified expert testimony and proof beyond a reasonable doubt were satisfied.
key_cases.relevance: Addresses the father's challenge that placement was not decided until after the termination hearing, under the Iowa ICWA placement framework.
key_cases.quote: Even assuming the issue was properly preserved, we conclude active efforts were made to prevent the breakup of the Indian family.
